| D-11 | Signature visual: the braid | Three-strand fusion motif is the brand mark. Frozen channel colours used everywhere (docs, README hero, explorer, CLI, benchmark charts): purple #7F77DD = vector, teal #1D9E75 = conceptual (brand accent — the differentiator carries the brand colour), coral #D85A30 = graph. Result-level provenance = three-chip strip, opacity = channel contribution. Benchmark visual = rank-braid (bump/alluvial) showing channel rankings weaving into the fused RRF ranking. 3D conceptual explorer becomes the click-through triptych (vector cloud / dimension-polygon overlap / graph ego-network). | Confirmed 2026-08-29 |

| D-12 | Brand, positioning & launch narrative | Aha: "You search in words. You choose in qualities." Brand essence: judgement with receipts — (1) business-defined dimensions give software judgement; (2) explanation-by-decomposition + radical evidential honesty (GOV-01, published losses, retracted-claims founding story) are the receipts. Tagline: "Search that knows what better means." Voice: the honest engineer — no superlatives, always artefacts; business value framed as hypotheses until US5 benchmarks land. Category claim: the semantic layer for hybrid retrieval. Positioning: for developers building search over attribute-rich data who find similarity can't rank by graded qualities, KSE is an open-source substrate that lets the business define "better" and fuses it with embeddings + graph, explainably, on CPU. Beachhead: e-commerce/product search; expansion via domain packs. Vector/graph DBs are backends not rivals; Elastic/Vespa/Weaviate hybrid = no conceptual channel; Alexandria = consultancy vs pip-installable; Rainbird = rules vs geometry. Flagship launch asset: side-by-side slider demo (vector-only vs KSE, live dimension sliders reordering results with D-11 chip strips). Discovery uses true Mom Test questions (past behaviour, no pitching). | Confirmed 2026-08-29 |

| D-13 | Universal framing (supersedes D-12 beachhead clause) | Identity is the universal substrate — any industry, FS or non-FS; no domain owns it. Universal aha: "Every expert ranks by qualities their tools can't see. KSE lets any organisation encode its own definition of better." Tagline unchanged (already domain-neutral). Explainer examples rotate across domains (credit analyst / lawyer / clinician / procurement / merchandiser). FS elevated as a proof-point domain: explanation-by-decomposition doubles as audit/suitability evidence (Consumer Duty, model-risk auditability) — "receipts" is a compliance artefact in FS. Go-to-market nuance retained: universality is proven, not claimed — flagship demo becomes SAME ENGINE, TWO SCHEMAS, SWAPPED LIVE (FS instrument screening + product search on one substrate, different YAML). Domain packs (US6: retail, finance, docs) are proof points of the universal claim, not verticals of identity. All launch copy audited for domain-neutral identity language. | Confirmed 2026-08-29 |
| D-14 | Inspection: all flavours, user's choice | Receipts must be openable with ordinary tools. Layers: (1) CLI built-in — kse stats / show <id> / explain "<query>" with D-11 chip strip via rich (lands with FR-02; needed to debug the scorer); (2) Datasette over the SQLite store — zero-code web UI, documented one-liner; (3) notebooks BOTH flavours — Jupyter packs with US6 (reach), marimo flagship with T-057 (reactive sliders = D-12 aha natively; git-friendly .py); (4) to_dataframe()/to_parquet() escape hatch — polars/DuckDB/Excel; (5) graph-native — Neo4j Browser/Bloom on T1, kse export --graphml for Gephi/yEd on NetworkX; (6) kse dashboard triptych built as one artefact with the T-057 demo, not separately. Design constraint on FR-02: dimension scores + hashes stored as plain queryable SQLite columns, never pickled blobs — inspectable by construction. | Confirmed 2026-08-29 |
| D-15 | Data platform integration strategy | Projection-first posture (D-08) = native fit for warehouse/lakehouse. Tier 1 universal interchange: Parquet + Arrow ingest/egress + DuckDB local engine — covers Snowflake, Databricks, BigQuery, Fabric/OneLake, Delta, Iceberg with zero vendor SDKs. Tier 2 (demand-driven connectors): Snowflake (Snowpark), Databricks (databricks-sql), BigQuery. Tier 3: CDC streaming (Kafka/Debezium → FR-01 incremental upsert; content hash makes ingestion idempotent by construction), orchestrator operators (Airflow/Dagster/Prefect), dbt integration (dimension scoring in the transform DAG; schema versioned beside dbt models). Egress unlock: write dimension scores + provenance back as plain platform tables — sliders become SQL columns, joinable in BI, audit trail lives where auditors look. CPU-first (D-03) enables in-platform compute (Snowpark Containers, Databricks CPU clusters, Fabric notebooks) with no GPU provisioning. | Confirmed 2026-08-29 |


| D-16 | Unit testing strategy | Five lanes (guardrail/unit/component/integration/conformance); real-local-backends over mocks — mocks only at true external boundaries; deterministic stub embedder (real interface implementation) for offline lanes + cached genuine ONNX lane; Hypothesis property tests mandatory for hash/RRF/schema invariants; zero flake tolerance; diff-cover ratchet; legacy mocked tests deleted per-FR with hard-fail flip at Phase 2 completion (T-015). Full text: docs/TESTING.md. | Confirmed 2026-08-29 |
| D-101 | Local model cache location | Default embedding model resolves from `~/.cache/kse/models/<model_id>/model.onnx`. Precedence: `KSE_CACHE_DIR` > `XDG_CACHE_HOME/kse` > `~/.cache/kse`. Resolution is pure — never creates directories, never downloads (AR-01). Namespaced by model id so a model upgrade cannot silently reuse a stale artefact, since the id is part of projection replay identity. | Confirmed 2026-08-29 |

| D-102 | TC-02 "no network call" ruling | The one-time, documented, out-of-band model fetch satisfies TC-02. The clause binds every *run* of the default path — quickstart, ingest, query, scoring — all of which execute under the no_network fixture in CI with the genuine model. Fetching the model is setup, not a run, and is never performed by KSE code (AR-01 has no download path by construction). Ruled by the maintainer, 2026-08-30; unblocks T-025/T-029. | Confirmed 2026-08-30 |

**Numbering:** the BD sessions own the sequential range (D-01…). Decisions originated on the Claude Code parallel track use **D-101+** so the two tracks cannot collide — D-11 and D-14 both collided before this was adopted.
